summary: Tested the security audit fixes: public tracking privacy, the last-4-digit unlock with lockout, order-token gating for window/rating/share, and signed file links. Backend: 14 new pytest cases in tests/test_order_privacy_security.py all pass (100%). A serial run of the full suite was cut off at about 37% by the 290s tool limit, with no failures up to that point. Frontend: every requested flow works on the live preview. That covers the customer index (codes + STOP n, no names), the public tracking page (ETA, stops away, driver first name, MANAGE THIS ORDER box, no address), wrong digits giving verify-error, and 0100 unlocking the address and window picker. A window booking (today 18-20) saved and persisted. On a delivered order the proof photo and signature load through the signed URL, the share link opens /api/proof/{token} and its image loads, a 2-star rating shows apology-code, and a 4-star rating shows no code. The driver stop screen pod-photo-saved image loads with ?t=<session>. Found 1 functional bug (a staff user gets signed out after entering wrong digits) and 2 layout/keyboard issues on small screens.

minor.issue: With an X-Order-Token these return the full Stop model_dump (customer_phone, notes, pod_photo_path, share_token, fail_reason, merchant_* fields, fee). The token holder is the customer, but it is wider than order_private(). Consider returning public_stop() + order_private() instead.

The per-code limit (10 tries across all IPs) means anyone who knows a tracking code can lock the real customer out for 15 min. This is an accepted brute-force trade-off; it is listed here only so it is a known decision.

ui_bugs.issue: A staff session (admin/driver) already loaded in memory gets wiped when a wrong last-4 is entered on /customer/{code}. /track/{code}/verify returns 401, and api.ts:105 calls clearSession() for any 401 when a token exists (only /auth/login is excluded). Reproduced: admin signed in -> /admin -> in-app nav to /customer/MD1004 -> enter 9999 -> localStorage multidrop_session removed. A wrong or expired X-Order-Token (401) on window/rating/share/private would do the same. Fix: skip clearSession for /track/ paths and for requests that send X-Order-Token, or only clear when the 401 detail is a session error.

issues: The tracking sheet is a plain View, not a ScrollView. Once the order is unlocked and delivered (address + proof + share + rating prompt with tags), the sheet is taller than the screen. The map collapses to 0 height and the absolute DELIVERED banner overlays the header, and rating-submit-button sits at y=647-703 in a 667px viewport. On native (no body scroll) the submit button is cut off and can't be reached. Wrap the sheet content in a ScrollView or give the map a minimum height.
No KeyboardAvoidingView on the tracking screen. verify-last4-input sits at the bottom of the sheet, so the iOS number-pad will cover the input and the UNLOCK button.
Window day/slot chips (customer-window-day-*, customer-window-slot-*) are 36px tall, below the 44px touch-target minimum.

action_items: api.ts: don't call clearSession() on 401 from /track/{code}/verify, /track/{code}/private or requests carrying X-Order-Token (wrong digits currently sign staff out).

customer/[code].tsx: make the bottom sheet scrollable (ScrollView) or cap its height, so the rating submit, proof and window picker stay reachable on small phones; add KeyboardAvoidingView for the last-4 input.
Optional: return a trimmed payload (public_stop + order_private) from PUT /stops/{id}/window and POST /stops/{id}/rating instead of the full Stop model.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3455 lines; it should be split into routers (tracking/auth/merchants/routes).

require_order_access checks the order token first and gives a clear 401/403; file_allowed accepts the file token only for the exact path and the staff session only for an existing, enabled user, and an order token is correctly rejected for files (verified).
client_ip uses the last X-Forwarded-For hop, which is correct behind the ingress, so the per-IP limit can't be dodged by spoofing XFF.
customer/[code].tsx: the /private refresh .catch(() => setOrder(null)) re-locks the order on any network blip, not only on token expiry. Minor.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows; 1 medium bug + small-screen layout issues

seed_data_creation: Delivered MD1002 (photo + signature) and MD1003 (signature) as drv-1 during testing. Ran POST /api/admin/reset afterwards and cleared db.login_attempts trk* keys.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with -n0 and export EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (older suites read it from the env). The new suite reads phone digits straight from Mongo (db.stops.customer_phone) and cleans trk* login_attempts. MD100N phones are +1415555010(N-1), so MD1002 -> 0101 and MD1003 -> 0102. Web session lives in localStorage 'multidrop_session' ({token,user}); inject it to test driver/admin screens.
rca_of_issue: Staff sign-out: api.ts treats every 401 as an expired staff session when getToken() is non-null. The new customer endpoints use 401 for 'wrong digits' and for a bad order token, so a signed-in staff user who mistypes is logged out. Repro steps are in ui_bugs. Mitigation: exclude the customer/order paths from the clearSession branch.
